tech_stack.architecture: Single-file monolith on App Runner with shared MySQL/RDS

findings.title: No machine-readable API specification
findings.description: 22 JSON endpoints are declared only as inline string/regex comparisons on $request_uri in index.php. No OpenAPI, Swagger, GraphQL, AsyncAPI or Smithy file exists; searched for openapi.*/swagger.*/*.graphql/*.smithy across the repo (7 files total) and in the dependency surface (no composer.json).
findings.gap: Agent tool definitions must be hand-authored from source reading and will drift from implementation.
findings.recommendation: Generate an OpenAPI 3 document for the /api/* surface and validate it in CI against the route table.

findings.title: Errors are unstructured single-string bodies
findings.description: All failures return {"error": "<message>"} with no error code, category or retryable flag; several handlers echo raw exception text (http_response_code(500); echo json_encode(['error' => $e->getMessage()])).
findings.gap: An agent cannot distinguish retriable from terminal failures and raw exception text may leak internals.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a shared error envelope with code, message, retryable and field-level details; stop echoing exception messages.

findings.title: Write endpoints are not idempotent
findings.description: POST /api/orders mints uniqid('order-') per call and decrements inventory; POST /api/returns, /api/admin/approve-return and the eight fulfillment POSTs accept no idempotency key and perform no duplicate detection. Retrying any of them creates a second order, a second refund payment row, or a second inventory restore.
findings.gap: No idempotency key support, no unique business-key constraint, no replay detection.
findings.recommendation: Accept an Idempotency-Key header on every POST, persist it with a unique index, and return the original response on replay.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND no idempotency mechanism on any write endpoint.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: has_write_operations=true (POST/PUT/DELETE order, return, refund and user endpoints), so a retried agent call duplicates orders, refunds and inventory movements.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Add an idempotency_keys table and wrap POST /api/orders and /api/admin/approve-return first.
blocker_remediation.target_state: All state-mutating endpoints are replay-safe under a caller-supplied key.

findings.title: Responses are flat JSON via json_encode
findings.description: Every /api/* handler sets Content-Type: application/json and serialises associative arrays with json_encode; no XML, protobuf or binary payloads exist.
findings.gap: Nested envelopes are inconsistent (some return {products:[...]}, others a bare object), so tool schemas must be written per endpoint.
findings.recommendation: Standardise on one response envelope shape before generating agent tools.

findings.title: No event emission on state change
findings.description: Order status transitions are written only to the order_status_history table by update_order_status(). No webhook, SNS, EventBridge, SQS or Kafka integration appears in index.php or in infrastructure/monolith-apprunner.yaml.
findings.gap: Agents must poll /api/orders/{id}/history to observe transitions.
findings.recommendation: Publish an EventBridge event from update_order_status() for each transition.

findings.title: Rate limits neither enforced nor advertised
findings.description: The WAFv2 WebACL only IP-allowlists and applies AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputs; there is no rate-based rule, no App Runner throttle and no X-RateLimit-* or Retry-After header anywhere in index.php.
findings.gap: Agents have no self-throttling signal.
findings.recommendation: Add a WAF rate-based rule and emit X-RateLimit-Remaining/Retry-After.

findings.title: Only human session cookies; no machine identity
findings.description: The sole authentication path is POST /login with username/password against the users table, storing the row in $_SESSION. /api/* gates on isset($_SESSION['user']). There is no OAuth2 client-credentials flow, API key, mTLS, Cognito app client or App Runner/API Gateway authorizer in the CloudFormation template.
findings.gap: An agent can only authenticate by replaying a human user's password and cookie, so no call can be attributed to an agent principal.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a machine-identity path (OAuth2 client credentials or signed API keys bound to a principal) and record that principal on every request.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Add an agent service-principal table plus bearer-token middleware in front of /api/*.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Every API call carries a distinct, revocable machine principal recorded in logs.

findings.title: Authorization is role-coarse, not action-level
findings.description: Checks are binary string comparisons ($_SESSION['user']['role'] !== 'admin' / $current_user['role'] !== 'admin') on five admin endpoints; every other /api/* route is open to any logged-in user. The admin role implies create, update and delete on users, returns, refunds and all fulfillment transitions with no sub-division.
findings.gap: No permission matrix allows read-without-delete, so an agent needing admin reads inherits refund and user-deletion power.
findings.recommendation: Replace the role string check with a per-action permission map evaluated in a single middleware.

compensating_controls: Restrict the pilot agent to the customer role and read-only routes
Front /api/admin/* with a separate gateway that denies agent principals

findings.title: No identity propagation or on-behalf-of mode
findings.description: Identity exists only as a PHP session array; there is no JWT parsing, no token exchange, and no X-User-Id style header handling. changed_by on status history is set to the literal session username, 'system' or 'carrier', so an agent acting for a user is indistinguishable from the user.
findings.gap: Agent-as-self and agent-on-behalf-of-user cannot be separated, which is a privilege-escalation path.
findings.recommendation: Carry a JWT with distinct actor and subject claims and persist both on every write.

compensating_controls: Give the agent its own dedicated low-privilege user row so its writes are at least separable
Require the orchestration layer to record the human requester outside the app

findings.title: Database credentials passed as plaintext environment values; demo passwords in source
findings.description: The App Runner service injects DB_USER/DB_PASS as RuntimeEnvironmentVariables from NoEcho stack parameters rather than from Secrets Manager; no AWS::SecretsManager::Secret or rotation resource exists in the template. index.php falls back to the literal 'ecommerce_pass' when DB_PASS is unset, and the login page renders working demo credentials (customer/customer123, admin/admin123) seeded by seed_data().
findings.gap: No secrets manager, no rotation, and a hardcoded fallback password plus published demo credentials.
findings.recommendation: Move DB credentials to Secrets Manager with rotation (or RDS IAM auth, already enabled on the instance), delete the hardcoded fallback, and remove the demo credential block.

compensating_controls: Rotate and remove the seeded demo accounts before any agent pilot
Switch the connection to EnableIAMDatabaseAuthentication, which the RDS instance already supports

findings.title: Write audit trail is mutable application data
findings.description: The only write trail is the order_status_history row inserted by update_order_status() with a changed_by string; it lives in the same MySQL schema the API can UPDATE/DELETE. There is no AWS::CloudTrail::Trail, no log-file validation, no S3 Object Lock and no audit record at all for user create/update/delete, return approval or refund issuance.
findings.gap: No immutable, tamper-evident record of agent-initiated writes, and whole classes of writes are unlogged.
findings.recommendation: Emit an append-only audit record (CloudWatch Logs with retention/KMS, or an Object-Lock S3 sink) carrying the authenticated principal for every mutating call, and enable CloudTrail on the account.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled and the only write log is mutable in-schema data.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: has_auth_surface and has_write_operations are both true, so the surface-flag INFO downgrade does not apply; refunds and user deletions are unauditable.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Log principal, action, target and timestamp to a dedicated append-only CloudWatch log group on every write.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Tamper-evident audit coverage for 100% of mutating endpoints.

findings.title: No identity suspension path
findings.description: The only lifecycle controls are DELETE /api/admin/users/{id} (hard delete) and a role change via PUT. There is no disabled/suspended flag on the users table, no token or API-key revocation endpoint, and no session invalidation other than the user's own /logout.
findings.gap: A misbehaving agent identity can only be stopped by deleting the row or taking the service down.
findings.recommendation: Add an is_active column enforced in the /api/* auth gate plus an admin suspend endpoint.

compensating_controls: Use the WAF IPSet to cut the agent's egress IP as an emergency stop
Keep the agent's credential in a secret that can be rotated to revoke access

findings.title: No compensation across the multi-step fulfillment workflow
findings.description: Single requests are transactional (beginTransaction/rollBack in POST /api/orders and /api/returns), but the eight-step fulfillment sequence (validate → assign-warehouse → pick → pack → quality-check → ship → deliver) has no undo endpoint: assign-warehouse increments warehouses.current_load with no decrement path, and /ship writes carrier and tracking irreversibly. The only inventory/payment reversal is the human-gated POST /api/admin/approve-return.
findings.gap: No saga, no compensating transactions and no undo endpoints for cross-request sequences, so a failure at step 5 leaves partial state an agent cannot repair.
findings.recommendation: Expose explicit compensating operations (unassign-warehouse, void-shipment, cancel-order) and model the sequence as a saga with recorded step state.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled and multi-step write workflows have no compensation path.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: has_write_operations=true and the archetype is stateful-crud, so the INFO downgrades for stateless-utility / no-write surfaces do not apply.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Add unassign-warehouse and cancel-order compensating endpoints.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Every forward fulfillment step has a matching reversal callable by the agent.

findings.title: No concurrency control on shared rows
findings.description: Inventory is mutated with blind relative updates (UPDATE inventory SET stock_quantity = stock_quantity - ?) after a separate non-locking SELECT of stock_quantity; warehouse load uses the same read-then-write pattern. There is no version column, no ETag/If-Match handling and no SELECT ... FOR UPDATE anywhere in index.php.
findings.gap: Concurrent agent instances can oversell stock or drive status transitions out of order with no conflict detection.
findings.recommendation: Add an optimistic version column on orders/inventory and reject stale writes, or take row locks inside the existing transactions.

compensating_controls: Run a single agent instance with serialised execution during the pilot
Add a DB CHECK/constraint preventing negative stock_quantity as a backstop

findings.title: No rate limiting or throttling
findings.description: No application middleware limits request rate; the WAFv2 ACL contains only an IPSet allow rule and a managed bad-inputs rule; App Runner AutoScalingConfiguration sets MaxConcurrency 100 with MaxSize 3 but that is capacity, not a limit. There is no API Gateway or usage plan in front of the service.
findings.gap: A runaway agent loop can saturate the three App Runner instances and the db.t3.micro RDS instance.
findings.recommendation: Add a WAF rate-based rule per source and a per-principal application limiter.

compensating_controls: Keep the WAF IP allowlist narrow so only the agent egress IP can reach the service

findings.title: No business-level blast radius limits
findings.description: POST /api/admin/approve-return refunds the full order total with no per-hour or per-caller cap; POST /api/orders accepts an unbounded data['items'] array; the admin user endpoints have no cap on create/delete volume. No max_*_per_hour, bulk-size or spend threshold configuration exists in index.php or the template.
findings.gap: Only capacity-level protection exists; nothing bounds the business impact of a correct-but-catastrophic agent loop.
findings.recommendation: Add per-principal daily refund-amount and bulk-operation caps enforced server-side.

compensating_controls: Keep refund approval human-gated during the pilot (current behaviour)
Cap items-per-order and records-per-call at the orchestrator

findings.title: No formal data classification metadata
findings.description: Stage A = Yes: MySQL stores customer name, email, shipping address, payment rows and bcrypt password hashes. B1 is clear — GET /api/admin/users explicitly projects id, username, name, email, role, created_at (password excluded) and login unsets $user['password'] before writing the session. B2 is clear — admin vs customer roles differentiate access to the admin data domain. B3 fired: no sensitivity tags on the RDS/ECR resources, no field-level annotations, and no Macie or equivalent detection.
findings.gap: No machine-readable classification, so agent tooling cannot programmatically identify which fields are sensitive.
findings.recommendation: Tag the RDS instance and annotate the users/orders/payments columns with sensitivity labels; consider Macie for the data store.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to INFO: B1 and B2 are clear, only B3 (formal classification metadata) fired.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: Password hashes are excluded from all agent-reachable responses and role-based differentiation exists, so the write-enabled BLOCKER path for B1 did not fire.

b1.reasoning: Password column omitted via explicit SELECT projection in GET /api/admin/users and unset() after login.

b2.reasoning: admin/customer roles gate the admin data domain; /api/orders/me is scoped to the session customer_id.

b3.reasoning: No classification tags, field annotations or PII detection tooling found in index.php or infrastructure/monolith-apprunner.yaml.

findings.title: No data residency or sovereignty controls
findings.description: The system persists customer names, emails and full shipping addresses (orders, users, interactions tables created in init_db). The CloudFormation template pins no region, declares no residency boundary, and there is no GDPR/LGPD/HIPAA reference, data-handling policy or egress restriction anywhere in the repository; the App Runner egress config allows HTTPS to 0.0.0.0/0.
findings.gap: Nothing constrains or documents where customer PII may be transmitted, so an agent forwarding order or customer records to an out-of-region LLM endpoint has no guardrail.
findings.recommendation: Document the residency classification for the orders/users data, pin deployment and any model endpoint to the approved region, and restrict egress to that endpoint.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled and the system holds customer PII with no residency control.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: has_persistent_data_store=true, so the INFO downgrade for no-data systems does not apply; archetype is stateful-crud, not stateless-utility.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Record the residency requirement for customer PII and pin the agent's model endpoint to the same region.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Documented, enforced jurisdiction boundary for all PII the agent can read.

findings.title: List endpoints are unbounded
findings.description: GET /api/products runs SELECT * FROM inventory, /api/orders/me and /api/orders/customer/{id} run SELECT * FROM orders ... ORDER BY created_at DESC, and /api/admin/orders/pending-fulfillment and /api/admin/users select whole tables. No limit, offset, cursor or filter parameter is accepted by any endpoint.
findings.gap: Agents receive whole tables, exhausting context and cost as data grows.
findings.recommendation: Add limit/cursor pagination with a server-side maximum page size to all list endpoints.

findings.title: Input validation is ad hoc and unstructured
findings.description: All SQL uses PDO prepared statements, but there is no validation library or middleware. POST /api/admin/users does only empty() presence checks and accepts any role string; POST /api/orders dereferences $data['items'] and $item['product_id'] with no shape, type or size validation; query parameters such as warehouseLoads and pickerStatus are json_decoded or array-consumed from $_GET unchecked. Validation failures return a single unstructured {"error": "All fields are required"}.
findings.gap: No field-level rejection signal, so an agent cannot self-correct a malformed payload; malformed items arrays raise untyped PHP errors instead of 400s.
findings.recommendation: Validate every request body against a schema and return field, constraint and message per violation.

findings.title: Timestamps present but not normalised or freshness-signalled
findings.description: orders, order_items history, returns, interactions and users carry created_at/updated_at DATETIME columns written with PHP date('Y-m-d H:i:s') in container-local time — DATETIME stores no offset and no UTC normalisation or NTP configuration is declared. No Cache-Control, X-Data-Age or consistency_level signalling appears on any response.
findings.gap: Agents cannot resolve timestamps to an absolute instant or tell whether a response is current.
findings.recommendation: Store UTC (or TIMESTAMP) and return ISO-8601 with offset plus explicit freshness metadata.

findings.title: No PII redaction in logs or error output
findings.description: ini_set('log_errors', '1') sends PHP errors to the Apache log with no scrubbing, and failures in the order/return/fulfillment paths echo raw $e->getMessage() to the caller. The validation-data endpoint returns customer name, email and address in its response body, and get_db() dies with the raw PDO connection error. No log filter, masking helper, CloudWatch metric filter or Macie integration exists.
findings.gap: Customer email, address and internal errors can reach logs and API responses unredacted, and then agent traces.
findings.recommendation: Add a redaction layer for log and error output, and stop returning exception text to callers.

compensating_controls: Scrub agent traces before persisting prompts/responses
Set a short retention period on the App Runner log group

findings.title: No data quality metric for the shared schema
findings.description: Ten tables are created inline by init_db() and populated by seed_data(); there is no profiling, null-rate monitoring, duplicate detection or freshness SLA. Three ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN calls wrapped in empty catch blocks run on every request, so column defaults ('Aisle 3-B', 1.5, '12x8x6') silently stand in for real warehouse data.
findings.gap: No completeness signal; placeholder defaults are indistinguishable from real values.
findings.recommendation: Profile the tables and track null/placeholder rates before letting an agent reason on warehouse and dimension fields.

findings.title: No schema or API versioning
findings.description: The schema is created by inline CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plus try/catch ALTER TABLE calls in init_db() — there is no migration directory, schema registry, JSON Schema, Avro or Protobuf definition. Routes are unversioned (/api/products, not /api/v1/products), no Accept-Version handling exists, and there is no changelog, deprecation notice or breaking-change detection (no CI configuration at all).
findings.gap: Any route or field change breaks agent tool bindings silently.
findings.recommendation: Introduce versioned route prefixes, a real migration tool, and OpenAPI diff checks in CI.

findings.title: No data catalog or metadata layer
findings.description: No Glue Data Catalog, DataHub/Collibra reference, data dictionary or schema documentation exists; the only description of the data model is the inline DDL in init_db() and the in-page note that MySQL is a shared database for orders, inventory, payments and returns.
findings.gap: Tool authors must read source to learn what the ten tables mean.
findings.recommendation: Publish a short data dictionary for the ten tables alongside the OpenAPI spec.

findings.title: No tracing and no structured logging
findings.description: Logging is limited to ini_set('log_errors','1') writing plain-text PHP errors to the Apache log. There is no OpenTelemetry or X-Ray SDK, no traceparent propagation, no JSON log formatting and no request_id/correlation_id generated or echoed by index.php. The CloudFormation template creates only a VPC Flow Log group and the implicit App Runner log group.
findings.gap: An agent-initiated failure cannot be correlated to server-side activity.
findings.recommendation: Emit JSON logs with a per-request correlation ID (accepting an inbound trace header) and add X-Ray or OTel instrumentation.

findings.title: No alarms on error rate or latency
findings.description: The template defines no AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm of any kind. Monitoring is limited to RDS enhanced monitoring (MonitoringInterval 60), WAF CloudWatchMetricsEnabled, and container HEALTHCHECK/App Runner health checks on '/'. There is no anomaly detection, SLO alerting or paging integration.
findings.gap: Degradation of the agent-facing API is detected only by the agent failing.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch alarms on App Runner 5xx rate and request latency, plus an RDS connection/CPU alarm.

findings.title: No business outcome metrics
findings.description: Only infrastructure telemetry exists (WAF rule metrics, RDS enhanced monitoring, VPC flow logs). No put_metric_data call, EMF output or custom dashboard tracks order conversion, fulfillment cycle time or return-approval rates — the metrics that would show whether agent actions produce good outcomes.
findings.gap: No outcome signal for agent effectiveness.
findings.recommendation: Publish custom metrics for orders placed, fulfillment transitions and refunds approved, dimensioned by principal.

findings.title: IaC present but no change review or drift detection
findings.description: infrastructure/monolith-apprunner.yaml defines the full agent-facing surface as code (VPC, RDS, ECR, two scoped IAM roles, WAF, App Runner service) — sub-check 1 passes. Sub-check 2 fails: there is no pipeline or PR gate; deploy.sh is a local docker-compose script and the template's own instructions tell operators to run aws cloudformation update-stack by hand. Sub-check 3 fails: no AWS Config rules or drift detection are declared.
findings.gap: Two of three governance controls are missing, so changes to the integration surface are unreviewed and undetected.
findings.recommendation: Deploy the template through a reviewed pipeline with change sets and enable drift detection/Config rules.

findings.title: No CI/CD pipeline or contract testing
findings.description: Searched for .github/workflows, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, buildspec.yml and CodePipeline resources in the template — none exist. The only build path is deploy.sh, which runs docker-compose build/up locally and curls /api/products. No Pact tests, OpenAPI validation or breaking-change detection exist.
findings.gap: API-breaking changes reach production undetected.
findings.recommendation: Add a pipeline that builds the image, runs API tests and diffs the OpenAPI spec before deploying.

findings.title: No defined rollback path
findings.description: Deployment is a manual update-stack with an ImageUri parameter; ECR ImageTagMutability is IMMUTABLE and keeps 10 images (so a prior artifact exists), but no blue/green config, CodeDeploy rollback trigger, canary, traffic shifting or feature-flag mechanism is defined. Recovery depends on an operator re-running update-stack with a previous tag.
findings.gap: No automated, time-bounded rollback for a change that breaks agent-facing routes.
findings.recommendation: Automate rollback by pinning the previous image tag in a pipeline stage with an automated health gate.

findings.title: No automated API tests
findings.description: The repository contains seven files and no test directory, test framework dependency or test file (searched for *test*, phpunit, Postman collections). The only verification is the single curl -f http://localhost:8080/api/products smoke check in deploy.sh.
findings.gap: No coverage of input handling, output shape, error responses or edge cases on the 22 agent-facing endpoints.
findings.recommendation: Add a PHPUnit or Newman API suite covering the fulfillment state machine and error paths, run in CI.

evaluations.title: Documented API Interface
evaluations.reason: A REST/JSON surface exists: 22 /api/* routes in index.php (products, orders, returns, fulfillment, admin users) returning application/json. Integration does not require direct DB access, file exchange or UI automation.

evaluations.title: Asynchronous Operation Support
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — all handlers are short synchronous DB operations; no workflow exceeds 30s and no long-running job surface exists.

evaluations.title: Scoped Permissions (Least Privilege)
evaluations.reason: The template uses two separate purpose-scoped IAM roles with inline least-privilege policies (logs writes scoped to the service log group; ECR pull scoped to the repository ARN) rather than wildcards or managed broad policies, and the app differentiates admin vs customer access. The mechanism to scope a caller identity exists.

evaluations.title: Queryable Current State
evaluations.reason: State is readable before acting: GET /api/orders/me, /api/orders/customer/{id}, /api/orders/{id}/history, /api/admin/orders/pending-fulfillment and the validation/picking/packing/shipping context endpoints, plus a status column on orders.

evaluations.title: Circuit Breakers and Resilience
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — the monolith calls no downstream services or external APIs; its only dependency is its own MySQL database.

evaluations.title: Graceful Degradation Signaling
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no priority was supplied (no P0 designation) and the repository declares no critical-path role.

evaluations.title: Draft/Pending State
evaluations.reason: Reviewable intermediate states exist: returns are created with status 'pending_review' and only committed by POST /api/admin/approve-return; orders pass through pending/confirmed/validated states before irreversible steps.

evaluations.title: Configurable Approval Gates
evaluations.reason: Explicit human approval endpoints exist and are role-gated: POST /api/admin/approve-return gates refunds, and POST /api/orders/{id}/validate and /quality-check take an approved/passed decision before the workflow advances.

evaluations.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
evaluations.reason: docker-compose.yml plus deploy.sh stand up the full app and MySQL locally, and seed_data() populates production-shaped users, inventory, warehouses and a sample order with items and payment.

evaluations.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
evaluations.reason: Schema and response fields are readable English (customer_email, shipping_address, stock_quantity, tracking_number, refund_amount, estimated_delivery_days); no legacy coded abbreviations requiring a dictionary.

evaluations.title: Encryption at Rest
evaluations.reason: The RDS MySQL instance sets StorageEncrypted: true and the ECR repository uses EncryptionType KMS with a customer-managed key (EnableKeyRotation true); the VPC flow log group is also KMS-encrypted.

items.summary: Establish machine identity and immutable audit, make writes replay-safe, add compensating operations for the fulfillment saga, and bound PII jurisdiction. No agent deployment — including pilots — should proceed before these close.

Close the safety cluster: action-level authorization and identity suspension, secrets in Secrets Manager, concurrency control, rate and business-transaction limits, and PII redaction in logs and error output.
Make the surface agent-consumable: OpenAPI spec, structured errors and validation, pagination, versioning, correlation IDs and alarms, and a reviewed pipeline with rollback.
Design inputs and hardening: response envelope consistency, event emission, rate-limit headers, classification tags, data dictionary, business metrics and API test coverage.

recommended_actions.action: Introduce machine identity with immutable audit attribution
recommended_actions.rationale: Session-cookie login is the only auth path, so no call can be attributed to or revoked for an agent principal, and the only write trail is mutable in-schema data.

recommended_actions.action: Make write endpoints replay-safe and reversible
recommended_actions.rationale: Retries duplicate orders and refunds, the eight-step fulfillment sequence has no undo, and inventory is mutated without locking.

recommended_actions.action: Bound blast radius and PII exposure before any pilot
recommended_actions.rationale: Customer PII has no residency boundary or log redaction, and nothing caps request rate, refund volume or bulk operation size.

recommended_actions.action: Publish a machine-readable contract and structured errors
recommended_actions.rationale: Tool definitions must currently be reverse-engineered from inline route matching, and unstructured errors prevent agent self-correction.

recommended_actions.action: Add a reviewed pipeline with API tests, alarms and rollback
recommended_actions.rationale: Deployment is manual update-stack with no tests, no drift detection, no alarms and no automated rollback for agent-breaking changes.
